message.content: {"rationale":"The supplied approximate collisions motivate testing whether drift at similar x and zero input depends on signed input history. The candidate input-trace account and the unsigned squared-input account respond differently to matched positive and negative pulses: their latent traces have opposite signs under signed filtering but are equal under squared-input filtering. Use equal-magnitude, equal-duration pulses with opposite signs, then a common zero-input interval. The measured x values may not match, so interpret slope differences cautiously.","hypotheses":["r1_b0","r2_b1"],"claim_under_test":"At comparable x with u=0, does the drift reflect a signed exponentially decaying trace of prior input, or an unsigned exponentially decaying trace of input magnitude squared?","expected_separation":"For the equal-magnitude opposite-sign pulses, r2_b1 predicts equal latent exposure traces, whereas r1_b0 predicts opposite-signed residual input traces and therefore potentially different drift. Both models also depend on x, so imperfect matching can obscure the distinction.","comparison_time":5.0,"matching_tolerance_x":0.04,"actions":[{"points":[[0,0],[0.5,1],[2.5,0]]},{"points":[[0,0],[0.5,-1],[2.5,0]]}],"failure_of_design":"The opposite pulses may produce x values too far apart at 5 seconds for a useful comparison. The models' x-dependent contributions and observation noise may then dominate the predicted history effect; even a close match may be inconclusive if the residual latent contributions have decayed or are too small."}
